date_note: Date is the company's announcement of 20 November as reported by Cybersecurity.com (Japan) on 24 November; the page gives no date for the intrusion itself.
title: McDonald's Japan says a third party accessed its official app database without authorization
summary: Cybersecurity.com (Japan) reports that McDonald's Japan announced on 20 November that a third party gained unauthorized access to its official app database. The affected data is purchase history, a customer management ID, IP addresses and device location information; the company says names, email addresses, phone numbers, addresses and card information registered in the app are not included. The company says it is invalidating the credentials used and reporting to the Personal Information Protection Commission.
plain: McDonald's Japan says someone without authorization accessed its app database. Per the company, purchase history, IP addresses and device location were involved, but not names, emails or card details.
exec: McDonald's Japan says app purchase history and location data were accessed without authorization; the company gave no count of people affected.
action: McDonald's Japan says it does not currently ask users to take special steps such as changing passwords, and will post updates if there is new information.

validation.note: One publisher (Cybersecurity.com Japan) reporting the company's 20 November notice; the company's own page could not be found and was not read. The article gives no figure for people or records affected.
